tactics.tactic: Tighten hook delivery to 0-2 seconds: voiceover word 1 must fire at or before second 1, bold on-screen text must be visible at frame 1. The 5.8s average swipe means you have a 2-second window, not a 3-second window. Enforce this as a hard production rule: any Short where voice or text appears after 2 seconds gets re-cut.
tactics.why: vidIQ data: hooks at 2s or earlier retain 19% more viewers; average swipe happens at 5.8s. Every second of delay past second 2 compounds viewer loss before they've heard the hook.
test_ideas: Text + voice at 0s vs text at 0s + voice at 1s vs text at 0s + voice at 2s — measure 'Viewed vs Swiped Away' differential
5-word text overlay vs 8-word text overlay at frame 1 (shorter may read faster on autoplay)
Result-reveal hook ('Babies remember this forever') vs shock-stat hook ('73% of parents get this wrong')

tactics.tactic: Run a weekly 3-hook A/B test: produce 3 hook variants for the same fact body, post as 3 separate Shorts on the same channel within the same week. Review 'Viewed vs Swiped Away' in YouTube Studio at 48 hours. Only scale the format of the top-performing hook into the next week's content batch.
tactics.why: vidIQ explicitly recommends testing 3 hooks per week; Viewed vs Swiped Away 70%+ is the stated KPI threshold. Systematic testing is the only way to improve hook performance without guessing.
test_ideas: Hook variant A: result-first ('The coin worth $50,000') vs B: curiosity-gap ('Most people throw this coin away') vs C: question-format ('Is your old coin worth a fortune?')
Visual hook: AI image of the result vs AI image of the problem
Track 'Viewed vs Swiped Away' not just views — set 70% as pass/fail threshold

tactics.tactic: For monetization optimization, prefer 25-35 second Shorts targeting 85-90% completion over 60-second Shorts targeting 50-60% completion. Following the March 2026 RPM update, shorter Shorts with near-complete watch-through generate more revenue per view than longer Shorts with mid-roll dropout. Design the idea first, then pick the shortest length at which the fact feels complete.
tactics.why: March 2026 update: 30s at 90% completion beats 60s at 50% completion for both distribution AND RPM. Completion rate now directly influences revenue — not just impressions — making length optimization a financial decision, not just algorithmic.
test_ideas: Same fact scripted at 20s vs 35s vs 60s — compare completion rate and estimated RPM after 500 views
Single-insight 20s loop vs 3-fact 60s compilation — track both view count and revenue per 1000 views
Monitor 'Average Percentage Viewed' in YouTube Studio: flag any Short under 70% for script/hook revision

tactics.tactic: Always add a one-line AI disclosure to every Short description: 'Visuals and voiceover created with AI.' This ensures disclosed AI content receives normal algorithmic distribution. Do not rely on YouTube's AI label alone — add explicit description text to avoid any manual review flag.
tactics.why: Creator Insider / YouTube official: properly disclosed AI content is not penalized. Undisclosed AI that gets flagged during manual review can face distribution throttling. This is a zero-cost protection step.
test_ideas: Confirm all existing channel templates include disclosure line in description template
No A/B test needed — this is a compliance step, not an optimization

tactics.tactic: Optimize posting time around your seed audience (niche-core viewers) rather than generic 'peak hours.' The two-phase explore/exploit system means the seed audience's completion rate in the first 6-12 hours determines whether broad distribution fires. Test posting at 9 AM vs 12 PM vs 7 PM per channel and track same-day 'Viewed vs Swiped Away' as proxy for seed quality.
tactics.why: Creator Insider confirmed the explore/exploit seed system. Weak seed engagement kills the video regardless of content quality. Posting when your specific niche audience is most active increases the probability of a strong seed signal.
test_ideas: BabyFactsUnlocked: test 9 AM vs 7 PM — parenting audience likely active at evening family time
MoneyFactsUnlocked: test 7 AM vs 12 PM — finance audience likely checks phone before/during workday
AI Facts Unlocked: test 10 AM vs 9 PM — tech audience skews toward late-evening scrolling
